workLog.phase: Drive the loop with a live scorer
actions: Anthropic is rate-capped until 2026-08-01, so routed through GitHub Models: EVAL_PROVIDER=github with openai/gpt-4o-mini, which scripts/eval/_providers.py already supports
Ran scripts/eval/eval-rule-activation.py live over all seven files in tests/evals/rule-scenarios/, 24 scenarios, into base-report.json
optimize-artifact.py extract --kind rule produced 24 tasks, 12 passing: real headroom rather than a saturated benchmark
split --seed live-2026-07-27 drew 14 opt and 10 sel; stdout published opt membership only, so sel stayed hidden as designed
Read the report filtered to the 14 opt ids only, printing '<HELD OUT, not read>' for the rest, to keep the optimizer role honest
workLog.outcome: First end-to-end run of the loop against a real model. Fingerprint 06f74397...

workLog.phase: Make a candidate edit and gate it
actions: Opt-visible diagnosis on .claude/rules/working-with-legacy-code.md: both visible failures scored 2.33 with the judge saying the behavior was right but 'lacks the expected vocabulary', and the rule bound its vocabulary only to 'PR descriptions and review comments'
Edited the rule: added a two-gate summary, a 'Say The Words' section binding the vocabulary to every surface, and a plain-refusal instruction for the non-activating case
Re-ran the live scorer and extracted cand.json
On the visible opt group the edit moved 6/14 to 7/14, and neither task it targeted flipped
gate returned ACCEPT: sel 0.6 to 0.8, 2 discordant gains, 0 losses, p=0.25, 1 consultation of 5
workLog.outcome: A held-out ACCEPT, which the loop is built to treat as the win condition.

workLog.phase: Distrust the ACCEPT and run a null control
actions: Post-hoc, the edited rule's own four scenarios had not moved at all: S1, S2, S3 still failing, S4 still passing. All three flips came from rules the edit never touched
That is not what a real improvement looks like, so restored the rule byte-for-byte (git diff empty) and re-ran the identical scorer as a null control
5 of 24 tasks flipped with no input change; the held-out group moved 6/10 to 7/10 on its own
Both sel gains that earned the ACCEPT also flipped under the null run, so the ACCEPT was variance, confirmed rather than suspected
Gating the byte-identical no-op returned REJECT, but only because noise had broken one task and the ADR-057 no-regression clause caught it
workLog.outcome: The verdict on this benchmark was decided by scorer variance, not by the edit. The real candidate got lucky; the no-op got unlucky.

actions: The gate already computed a one-sided exact McNemar tail and printed it, but nothing could act on it; the source comment said so explicitly
TDD: 16 core tests and 7 CLI tests written first, all failing for the right reason (no such parameter, then unrecognized argument)
Added max_p to gate() and --max-p to the gate subcommand, defaulting to absent so a small held-out group stays informative rather than unpassable
Ordered the bar last among accept-path refusals so a broken task is still the finding named first
Replayed both live runs under --max-p 0.05: the false ACCEPT became a REJECT naming the 0.25 tail, and the no-op stayed refused by the regression clause
workLog.outcome: 489 tests pass at this point in the session, 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules, ruff and mypy clean.

workLog.phase: Round fourteen adversarial review of the significance bar
actions: Ran the ADR Review Protocol on ADR-087 and the --max-p change with two non-Claude reviewers in parallel, per the adr-review skill: gpt-5.6-terra on the code, gemini-3.1-pro-preview on the ADR claims. Both returned REJECT. Multi-agent consensus on ADR-087 was not reached; the findings were adjudicated against data rather than accepted or dismissed wholesale.

Accepted all four blocking code findings. The load-bearing one was statistical: a per-comparison p threshold does not bound a family, so five consultations at 0.05 each is a family-wise 0.226. --max-p is now the family bar, Bonferroni-divided by --max-consultations.
Pinned max_p in the ledger like the consultation cap, including pinning its absence, so a candidate refused at 0.05 cannot be re-gated at 0.1.
Moved --max-p range validation ahead of the ledger so a malformed flag no longer spends a consultation or hides behind an exhausted budget.
Made max_p without p_value or without max_consultations raise instead of accepting.

Falsified the ADR reviewer's headline finding empirically. It claimed the null-control flips were HTTP 429 errors scored as failures. Checked all three live reports: zero errored mechanism-runs out of 216 and no FAIL_JUDGE_ERRORS verdict. The mechanism is real but did not fire, so it was filed as #3474 rather than folded in or dismissed.
Filed #3475: providers never pass OpenAI's seed and never read back system_fingerprint, so paired re-runs cannot be made comparable.

Corrected three documentation contradictions the reviewers found: the README and ADR both still claimed p was reported and never enforced, and the debate log claimed a 21 percent per-task flip rate that one replication cannot support.
Added the confounded-variance disclosure to the ADR and debate log: the measured movement is the pipeline's, not the judge's, and this harness cannot separate them.
workLog.outcome: Four blocking findings closed, verified by replaying the 2026-07-27 live runs: the false ACCEPT is now refused naming both the family bar and the corrected per-comparison bar, and attempts to loosen the bar to 0.5 or drop it are refused without spending a consultation. 508 tests pass with 100 percent line coverage on all three optimizer modules. Code landed as a5791784c.

workLog.phase: Attack the rule finding with data already in the repository
actions: The rule-path noise finding rested on one benchmark and one replication, which is thin enough to be worth attacking. Checked whether any committed artifact already disagreed with it before spending on another run.

Found the architect spike holds two runs of claude-sonnet-4-6, both reports tracked at evals/architect-spike/reports/. Verified model_id and agent_prompt_sha matched and treated the pair as a null control. Did not check fixture_set_sha. That omission is what makes the rest of this phase wrong.
Ran the full extract, split, gate loop on that pair. Default configuration returned ACCEPT: held-out 0.0 to 0.667, two discordant gains, no losses, p=0.25.

Verified --max-p 0.05 over a five-consultation budget refuses the same comparison at the corrected 0.01, and that adding the bar late to a group opened without one is refused. This part stands: it exercises the ledger pinning on real artifacts regardless of what the artifacts mean.
Measured the same comparison on the critic and high-level-advisor spikes and reported twelve of twenty-four across the three agents. Withdrawn in the next phase.

Corrected my own earlier reading in the debate log. I had recorded the rule run's REJECT as the design working. It was luck: requirement 4 fires when noise breaks something and is silent when noise falls one way. Filed as defect shape 16. This correction stands on the rule-path data and does not depend on the agent claim.
Published the agent claim in commit bb98bf24a across the README, ADR-087, the debate log, and this session log. Retracted the same day; see the next phase.
workLog.outcome: WRONG, retracted the same day in the phase below. The agent-path null control was not a null control: the two runs disagree on fixture_set_sha, so the corpus changed along with nothing else I had checked. The twelve-of-twenty-four corroboration is withdrawn in full. What survives this phase is the defect shape 16 correction, which rests on rule-path data, and the --max-p ledger verification, which does not depend on what the reports measured.

workLog.phase: Close the reviewer findings on PR #3478
actions: Three inline findings landed on PR #3478, two from Copilot on this session log and one from CodeRabbit on the causal graph. All three were correct.
endingCommit was empty while changesCommitted read complete, so the log contradicted itself. Set to bb98bf24a. The validator emitted a WARN rather than a failure, which is why it survived.

The session-end validation evidence claimed 489 tests while a later phase claimed 508. Corrected the end-of-session evidence to 508, since that evidence has to report the final state. Left the 489 in the earlier phase, which was true at that point, and made the qualifier explicit rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

The causal graph attributed the false ACCEPT to scorer variance. That names one stage when the run cannot distinguish two: the response model and the judge are both gpt-4o-mini at temperature 0, and this harness passes no seed and reads back no system_fingerprint. Rewrote the label to name both stages and cite issue #3475.

The pre-push suite then refused the push. Node ids in the causal graph are content-derived, so rewriting a label without recomputing its id orphans the node: the next episode naming the same milestone would hash to a different id and append a second record, splitting the evidence. Repaired with scripts/maintenance/repair_causal_graph_ids.py.
workLog.outcome: All three findings closed. The id invariant test in tests/skills/memory/test_update_causal_graph.py caught the second-order breakage before it reached the remote, which is exactly what that test exists for. 96 tests pass in that file.

workLog.phase: Retract the agent-path claim and find the defect it exposes
actions: Pushed on the agent finding rather than banking it. Searched for prior art first and found scripts/eval/variance-control.py and a committed control run at evals/security-spike/control/20260531T184905Z-60538bcf/ from issue #1877: N=20 at temperature 0, verdict stable twenty times out of twenty, response text unique twenty times out of twenty.

Formed a hypothesis from it: the agent path's instability lives in the brittle free-text regex assertions, not the verdict. Measured per assertion across the paired runs. Verdict unstable in 9 of 16 cells, regex in 6. Hypothesis falsified, and the opposite of what #1877 suggested.
Chasing an inconsistency in that measurement, checked fixture_sha. All eight fixtures differ between the two architect runs. fixture_set_sha be99fa1b1180 against 26136df314d6.

Established the fixtures directory has exactly one commit, c81ac278f, dated after both runs, and that the committed fixtures hash-match run B exactly. Run A's corpus is unrecoverable, so the pair cannot be repaired.

Checked all six tracked spikes. The critic and high-level-advisor pairs match on fixture_set_sha but differ on agent_prompt_sha. No same-model pair in the repository agrees on both. There is no valid agent-path null control anywhere in the repo.

Retracted the claim in scripts/eval/README.md, ADR-087 (both the finding section and Validation Status), and the debate log, where the retracted section is kept intact under a banner because the retraction is the finding.

Named the defect: _fixture_set_sha's own docstring says it lets a report consumer verify two runs hit the same set, and optimize-artifact.py extract never reads it. The schema supplies the check and the tool that needs it discards it. Filed as defect shape 17 and folded into ADR-087 open requirement 12, which had already named the missing corpus identity as a budget concern.
workLog.outcome: A published claim is withdrawn within hours of publishing it, and the withdrawal produced a real defect: the comparison tool ignores the field the report format provides to validate the comparison. Task ids are not a substitute, since all eight ids matched while the contents differed. Corrected state of the evidence: one path, the rule path, has a valid null control; the hook path needs none because pytest_results is deterministic; the agent path has none.

workLog.phase: Build the corpus guard, then survive two reviews of it
actions: Implemented the corpus-comparability guard TDD. Wrote 18 tests first, confirmed 12 red, implemented an envelope format optimizer-results/1 carrying {schema, corpus, results}, and made gate refuse a pair whose corpora disagree. Reader accepts legacy bare mappings; the discriminator is a string-valued schema key, not the key alone, so a legacy file with a task named schema still parses as legacy.

Proved the guard against the real incident rather than a fixture. Extracted the two tracked architect reports through the new extract, confirmed they emit different corpus values, and gated them exactly as the false accept was produced. REJECT, compared false, consultations 0, no ledger file written.

Round 15 adversarial review with gpt-5.6-terra returned REJECT with three findings, all real. CRITICAL: the guard was reachable by deletion, since stripping the envelope off either side left two unknowns and unknowns compared. REQUIRED: an unvalidated corpus string reported a verified match, so two reports both carrying an empty fixture_set_sha compared as verified. REQUIRED: reading both results files in full before the ledger lock let a malformed verdict mapping answer in place of an exhausted budget.

Closed the CRITICAL with two changes rather than one. split now pins the corpus of the results it was drawn from, so the value lives in the baseline commitment and no results file can delete it. And one known corpus beside an unknown one now counts as a conflict, which covers splits drawn before the pin existed. Neither alone is sufficient.
Closed the first REQUIRED by validating the corpus form as 64 lowercase hex at both the extraction boundary and the envelope reader.

Closed the second REQUIRED by splitting the read. The pre-lock work is now a header-only read that answers unknown to every content problem and cannot raise, wrapped in the digest scrubber. The full read moved into _gate_decision, after the ledger guards and before the charge.

Argued one point down rather than absorbing it. The reviewer wanted the whole corpus check moved behind the ledger lock. It stayed ahead: the file's convention, visible in the out-of-range --max-p check and the split-drift refusal, is that structural-validity refusals precede ledger refusals, and an incomparable pair is unusable at any budget. The reviewer's real concern was the full read, which the header-only split fixes.
Rewrote the test that encoded the bypass. The old assertion said unknown beside known compares; it now says that pair is refused. Bending the code to a stale test would have re-opened the CRITICAL.
Re-proved against the real data after the redesign. Both the original incident pair and the same pair with the candidate envelope stripped now return REJECT, consultations 0, zero ledger files.

Stated the bound in the README and the ADR rather than leaving it to be found. The split is caller-supplied and its pin sits outside the fingerprint, so a caller who edits two files together can still push an incomparable pair through. This defends against omission, not an adversary.

Recorded defect shape 18 in the debate log: a refusal reachable by deletion is not a refusal, and the generalization that a guard with a cannot-determine state should be measured by what it costs to reach that state deliberately.
workLog.outcome: 1050 tests pass with 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules. Ruff and mypy clean on changed files. The guard refuses the exact pair that produced the retracted claim, and refuses it again when the envelope is stripped.
evidence: uv run pytest tests/eval/ tests/test_eval_optimizer_core.py tests/test_eval_optimizer_adapters.py: 1050 passed
gate on evals/architect-spike/reports/20260528T051601Z-70c6ae97 against 20260528T055934Z-5f4d8ad4: REJECT, compared false, consultations 0
same pair with the candidate envelope stripped to a bare mapping: REJECT, compared false, consultations 0

workLog.phase: Round 16 review: close five defects and correct a documented overclaim
actions: Second adversarial review of the corpus guard, gpt-5.6-terra, returned REJECT with five findings. Confirmed all five by running the code, not by reading it. Two CRITICAL, three REQUIRED.

CRITICAL 1, the documented property was wrong. README and ADR-087 both claimed the corpus refusal cannot be deleted. True of the results envelope, false of the split pin: deleting the split's corpus key leaves two agreeing results files and no disagreement to refuse. Did not take the reviewer's fix of requiring a pin before any ACCEPT, because a --tasks split pins nothing by construction and neither the rule nor the hook path publishes a corpus identity, so that rule would disable the gate for two of three artifact classes. Split the claim into two reported facts instead: corpus_verified for the two results agreeing, corpus_pinned for the split naming the corpus they carry.

CRITICAL 2, TOCTOU between the header preflight and the full read. The two reads were never reconciled, so the values the comparison scored from never had to match the values the guard checked. The conflict rule now runs again against the loaded ResultsFile values, before the consultation is charged. Both call sites now emit one shared refusal payload so they cannot drift.
REQUIRED 3, split corpus pin was unvalidated. A split carrying corpus of [] raised TypeError out of a set comprehension. Now validated with the same 64-lowercase-hex check the results files get.

REQUIRED 4, _corpus_header promised it could not raise on content and caught only ValueError. A JSON array nested 200000 deep raises RecursionError, which escaped as an uncaught traceback ahead of the ledger guard. Normalized in both _read_json and _corpus_header.

REQUIRED 5, the preflight scrub test was tautological. It read capsys after _run_gate had drained it, and checked stderr while errors are emitted as JSON on stdout. Rewrote it against the returned payload and added a negative control that fails when the scrubber is removed.

TDD throughout: 18 new tests written first, 18 confirmed red, then implemented. Suite is 1081 passing with 100 percent coverage on optimize-artifact.py at 474 statements, _optimizer_core.py at 259, and _optimizer_adapters.py at 89.
Re-proved against the real incident pair three ways: pinned, candidate envelope stripped, and split pin deleted. All three REJECT with compared false, consultations 0, and zero ledger files written.

adr-review: ADR-087 requirement 5 rewritten from four properties to six, adding the pin-deletion limit and the recheck. The debate log records defect shape 19 and the reasoning for declining the reviewer's proposed fix.
workLog.outcome: Five review findings closed, one documented overclaim corrected rather than defended. Ruff and mypy clean on changed files, no em or en dashes in any changed file.
